text:
### Observed differences

- **The order between two groups of activities reversed.** In the earlier window, A26 came before A35, A36 and A41 in about 99–100 in 100 traces, and A27 came before each of the three in about 98–100 in 100. In the later window this is reversed: A35, A36 and A41 each come before A26 in about 99–100 in 100 traces and before A27 in about 98–99 in 100. All six activities still occur together in every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

- **Direct successors were rewired at the edges of the block.** Earlier, A25 passed about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A27; in the later window it splits roughly equally among A36, A41 and A35 (about 33 in 100 each), and A27 is almost no longer reached directly (under 1 in 100). Earlier, A26 spread its transitions over A41 (37 in 100), A35 (34) and A36 (28); in the later window about 99 in 100 go to A30. The trio's transitions into A30 (about 28–37 in 100 each earlier) nearly disappeared, replaced by transitions into A27 (about 31–34 in 100 each). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

- **Relative positions shifted in opposite directions.** A35, A36 and A41 now occur earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.58–0.59 before, about 0.41 after), while A26 (about 0.53 → 0.62) and A27 (about 0.38 → 0.47) occur later; the spacing between A27 and A26 stays similar (about 0.15 of the trace in both windows). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

- **Step distances moved consistently with the rerouting.** The gap from A25 to A27 grew from 1 step in about 99 in 100 traces to about 4–5 steps (about 93 in 100 at distance 4); the gap from A26 to A30 shrank from about 4 steps (about 93 in 100) to 1 step (about 99 in 100). A26 was followed within five steps by A35, A36 or A41 in 200 of 200 traces earlier but in only 1 of 200 later; A25 was followed by A35 within five steps in 1 of 200 traces earlier and 199 of 200 later, and A35 by A27 in 1 of 200 earlier and 199 of 200 later (the distance profiles on the sparse side of these items rest on only 1–2 observations). [LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG002, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block formed by A35, A36 and A41 — still executed together, in varying internal order — and the segment containing A27 and A26 exchanged their order. In the earlier window the flow ran A25 → A27 → … → A26 → one of A35/A36/A41 → A30; in the later window it runs A25 → one of A35/A36/A41 → A27 → … → A26 → A30, so the trio now executes between A25 and A27 where it previously ran between A26 and A30. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG003, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Supporting signs: screening tested 126 control-flow units and 26 items qualified, where about 0.6 would be expected if nothing had changed, so the ensemble is far beyond what an unchanged process produces; the six relation items show the reversal directly for every cross-pair between the two groups; the successor changes at A25, A26 and the trio, the complementary distance shifts and the opposite position shifts all describe the same rewiring; and participation and repetition are unchanged (each activity appears in essentially every trace, about once per trace, in both windows), which rules out the difference being merely a shift in how often existing paths are taken or in how often activities run. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

Limitations: no items cover the activities that run between A27 and A26, so the exact boundaries of the exchanged segments are inferred from the position and distance shifts; and the evidence shows that the two blocks exchanged order but cannot distinguish which side was moved — relocating the trio earlier and shifting the A27/A26 segment later produce identical traces. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, LAG001, LAG003]
